docs.inviting.component: `Inviting` is the LOOK of willingness: one coat a zone wears while a drag it would take is in
flight. Whether the zone is willing is never decided here — that is the `Acceptor`'s verdict —
and the tree carries no "highlighted" flag anywhere: grab dresses, release undresses, and the
undo puts back exactly what stood on the zone before.
```ts
import { node, Container, Acceptor, Inviting, wearInvites } from "game-kit"
const zone = node("sevens",
Container({ layout: "free" }),
Acceptor({ accept: { eq: ["el.values.rank", 7] } }),
Inviting({ coat: { recipe: "ring", level: 0.7, tint: "accent" } }))
// in the drag wiring:
const undress = wearInvites(root, grabbedCard)   // every willing zone puts its invite on
// …on release:
undress()                                        // and takes it off, exactly
## The verdict and the look are two different owners
`willingZones` asks the Acceptor and answers `allow` only — a request-gated drop is not an open
door. A game whose legality lives in its own functions (solitaire's runs, chess's moves) picks
the zones itself and uses the low door, `wearInvite(zone)`, one zone at a time. Either way the
invite goes into `Coated.self` — runtime state, exactly what that field exists for — so every
coat recipe a zone can wear (`ring`, `wash`, `fill`…) is already an invite recipe.
## A bare `Inviting()` already glows
The default coat is a stock ring in the accent. The three knobs — recipe, level, tint — are the
same three every coat has, so configuring the invite is configuring a coat, nothing new to learn.
docs.inviting.invite: A zone that takes SEVENS, and two cards you can drag at it. Pick up the seven and the zone puts
its invite on — ring, wash, whatever the knobs say; let go and it comes off, restoring whatever
the zone wore before. Pick up the eight and nothing lights: the rule answered `deny`, and an
unwilling zone has nothing to show. The knobs are the coat's own three — recipe, level, tint.
